answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card, adding one for each fatigue on that card; the Chairman adds one more. Modified 1–2 has no effect, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the officeholder: move the member to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal attrition.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a display card. Order them by descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. An acting player may peek at display blackmail. Do not refill during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. Then discard every remaining display card, refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), and return all unused Pensioners to supply.

At phase start check whether the opportunity marker matches the chosen main action. Take a main action once, or twice if it already matched; then move the marker to the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law can grant an extra action, which is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four offices vacant, Enlist Writer places one extra writer once this turn: a doubled Writer action therefore places three writers total.

After family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating as possible. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Seek Share payments go to the bank, not Company treasuries.

Fill vacant offices in ascending number on card backs. If promoting an officeholder, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card vacant into ascending hiring order. For own-family hiring, every other player represented in that office's candidate pool must verbally consent; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip it: office remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares). Shareholders may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody wins, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self, without Nepotism consent. The elected member's share moves to the Chairman slot and still counts for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.

Commit resources and cash first; for Company office checks, cash comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, roll, and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds, 3–4 fails and may retry if resources and office limits allow, 5–6 catastrophically fails and ends that office's actions, returning its officeholder to supply, discarding fatigue and flipping its card to Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or success chance (e.g. trade with no ship, deploy with no dice if no officer losses could result).

The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance needs consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); never move beyond the Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved within those limits; cash already in offices stays there.

Shipping must spend until £2 or less remains. Lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent; buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put acquired ships in any sea zone, including China if created. Extra ships return to supply at Refresh.

Declare the home region plus only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from that President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. On success, capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency's sea zone; ships are not exhausted. Fill as many as possible in declared regions, starting with a writer at home; later orders must extend this Trade's route, including via its filled-order tokens. Use all writers then tokens if needed; writers from another Presidency cannot extend the route. Do not fill another President's home, even if vacant. At most one successful Trade per President per turn (failures/retries occur in its uninterrupted chance). Gain Balance equal to listed order values, halved down for orders a firm filled this turn; President gets £1 per order and writer owners £1 per placed writer.

A Commander may target the Presidency home, an associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company target must have unrest or a closed order to make the action effective. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract target plus all other regions in its empire (count target once), with Company defense strength zero. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments never roll losses.

Loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of surviving participating officers plus one for the Commander; count only this attempt's surviving officers and used regiments/alliances. The Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Pay repeatedly in cycles: Commander £1 plus £1 per own used surviving officer; other families clockwise £1 per their used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment and each used alliance piece, until loot is gone. Then remove target tower/dome (and all matching flags if capital), open all target orders/remove unrest; on a new conquest put control token above associated President's box and Governor overlay in region, with only its card in Vacant Offices. If Governor General is in play, no Governor overlay/card is created. On catastrophe return half the Commander's family trophies rounded up and the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — success, payouts and control; catastrophe

answers.answer: Use the printed dice pool. Roll current pool without penalty, then reduce pool by one after every attempt regardless of result. On success take £1, or £2 if immediately previous roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one: ship stage, regiment, or tax. Each Build success places a partial ship in the region if none is there, or completes an existing partial ship into the President's associated sea zone. Commission a regiment into that President's Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Balance or that President's treasury; each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Every unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes Governor. Repeat while dice remain, or stop at will/catastrophe.

Company expenses are £1 per Debt, each Army officer/regiment and each ship in sea zones including China (not Commanders). If Balance is short, take £5 emergency loans; each raises Debt only if a track space remains, and at max Debt continue borrowing without advancing it. Set Balance to zero afterward. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Newly added emergency Debt adds no current expense. Compare remaining Balance to expectations for current Standing and lower Standing if short. Then Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per Company share, including its own; if total paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one. Standing reaching the leftmost space means failure.

For an attack on a Company region, resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary Rebellions in other unrest Company regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; within each Presidency its Commander orders associated regions. Primary normal Crisis strength is ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in target; primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die; each secondary attack strength is only that region's unrest cubes. The associated Commander chooses/exhausts pieces; if vacant, Military Affairs acts instead; if both vacant, Chairman acts. They exhaust active pieces equal to strength or as many as possible. Equal strength means attack fails/defense succeeds: remove all target unrest and Commander gains a trophy (and a defeated normal primary Invasion also removes one attacker tower if possible). Unequal means attack succeeds and Region Loss applies. The summary leaves unresolved how excess indivisible alliance strength counts, including strength-2 alliance vs strength-1 attack.
answers.evidence: Events — Crisis attacks on Company; Mounting defense; Unresolved counting boundary

answers.answer: A law passes at support 0 or higher: place it among passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy, then immediate law effects. At -1 or lower it fails: discard it, resolve dilemma's If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one space either way and resolves that adjacent policy. Restore all voting cards to regular orientation after either outcome. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call the special vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is starred. Use ordinary voting/support threshold, with exceptions: passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM passed-law token and activates firms; failing raises Company share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token (max ±3). No policy accompanies it; failure neither removes PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and PM may vote against. 1813 starts deregulated.

To form a firm, a player currently managing none returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to invested; flip their family board to firm charter, place a family member as first firm share, set value cube at leftmost, and take £5 from bank into London. Invest with manager consent using a Company share or workshop; each contribution puts £5 from bank into London and creates a firm share up to ten. Beyond ten it still adds £5 but no share. No Chairman share; no Company-share investment if Standing or Debt is lined; shares created this turn cannot be reinvested even if traded away. Invested workshops stay invested, losing bonus/failure VP even if firm fails.

Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn and needs at least one ship. Managers secretly choose trade zone/home port and commit a secret London bid, or Hobnob. Reveal bids together; reveal strategies at matching Presidency operations, before its actions; roll one die per £1 bid and pay bid to bank. At least one 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice; a President succeeding at Trade also gets initiative from Presidency ships. Fill lowest initiative first; President breaks ties, but if no successful President Trade, firms go after Commander/Governors and Chairman breaks ties. Fill only open orders, up to ships+1, start at strategy home and trace own route. Each firm cannot refill its own order that turn but can refill Company/another firm's; previously filled order pays half rounded down. Add revenue to India; advance Value one per full £6 added this turn.

At Revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, using London and/or India. If insolvent, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor's Prison (-1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards, charter back to family side; workshops stay invested. Rescue by emergency investments under normal share/workshop rules, or emergency merger with one firm. After expenses manager may dividend from India only: each dividend pays £1 per share plus £1 manager; a shareholder can waive only with manager consent. Record total actual cash paid out on Company Balance track; active non-Hobnob paying none records zero, Hobnob keeps prior marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.

Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Components are limited; when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. All information including discards and family cash is public except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids concealed during selection.

Negotiable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares, promise cards. Not negotiable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. To transfer a share, return old owner's family member and replace it at that location with a member of receiving family; adjust VP when luxury ownership changes. Facedown blackmail stays facedown when traded; faceup used blackmail cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are not, except a printed promise card's guaranteed effect can be called if possible. Follow a card's timing/limits, and make no promise calls during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. A transferred promise card may go to a third party or back to guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (e.g. a workshop already paid during Bonuses cannot pay again after a sale that phase).

Use the scenario's player setup cards and add three extra cards for five players or six for six, then shuffle and deal evenly. Place every listed holding: cash and enterprises in player area; office member/card in office; Company-share members in Court; writers/officers/trainees in indicated boxes; Commander in Army Commander slot without office card; each shipyard and matching ship in listed sea zone or unfitted on shipyard. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail into one deck and deal three display cards, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.

Game ends at scenario's final turn or Standing failure. Failure during Events in India finishes that phase before scoring; failure caused by legislation finishes the vote. During all Final Scoring stop negotiations and promise calls, and stop playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use.

Power counts enterprises and Company shares at their current track rates (bottom two positions are zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed card power (blackmail either side and applicable spouse). First/second awards by final turn: 3/1 on turns 1–3; 5/2 on 4–6; 8/4 on 7–8. Tied first each get only lower award, no other award; tied second get none. Highest VP wins; tie goes to most windows then clockwise from PM.

If Company survives, add current Court VP value per Company share; on failure subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Firm shares are scored in an earlier step: each player totals their shares across firms and rounds their total down once, then loses 1 VP per own family member in Debtor's Prison. In either outcome, eligible firm shareholders may make one special retirement from supply after firm scoring but before Power/ordinary scoring; no display cards. If Company survives, then roll office attrition and retire Pensioners without display cards. If failed, draw one random Company failure card instead of that ordinary final retirement/failure step.
answers.evidence: Scoring — Final Scoring order; Court/workshops; Final retirements/failure card

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately on taking a spouse. Retirement discounts stack, are personal, and each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring; discounts reduce actual spending and prestige priority. The summary does not enumerate individual spouse restrictions or scoring: read the relevant card.
If returned due to Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, a fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be bought while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.

Purchase Luxury: £4, gain luxury, 2 VP while owned and a window icon; social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard: £2, take it and put matching ship unfitted on shipyard; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop: £5, gain manufacturing enterprise, two votes and £1 bonus; worth 1 VP on Company failure if uninvested. Enlist Writer places a member in any Presidency Writers box (with at least four vacant offices, one extra writer once this turn); Enlist Officer puts member in Officers-in-Training. Seek Share pays £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5 to bank for the next empty Stock Exchange space; it is an applicant, not yet a share.
answers.evidence: Family — Family action table; New Company shares

answers.answer: If a family needs a piece and has none in supply, take one from any of its prizes and lose that prize's printed VP; applies to firm-share creation too. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns. Place a member from supply; if necessary, use one from a prize if possible and lose that prize's VP. If placement is impossible, there is no Chairman.

Chairman hires Director of Trade from current officeholders other than Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices vacant; Chairman also hires a writer for Manager of Shipping. Chairman chooses Military Affairs from a Presidential Commander, else any officer, else any Officer-in-Training. Director hires each President from a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with it. Associated President hires Governor from a writer or officer in region (not Commander). Chairman hires China Superintendent from any writer immediately when created. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way. Ordinary own-family choices require verbal consent from every other player in that office's candidate pool; Commander and Chairman appointments/elections are exempt.
answers.evidence: Hiring — office hirers and candidates; Nepotism

answers.answer: Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks: £1 treasury per die, no penalty. Each success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing its Superintendent overlay/card, after which Chairman hires any writer immediately. After envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones (including China once created). Transfers cannot occur until all envoys are finished.

Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers of an officer or regiment from one Army to another, keeping it in the top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army's top half. Finally appoint a Commander if a vacancy exists or a family has more total pieces in that Army than incumbent's family: choose a family with most pieces, move chosen officer to Commander slot and return former Commander to top as officer. A tie with incumbent's family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President chooses the order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; must give each a chance, though Commander/Governors may decline. Each position completes its actions before the next, and Trade cannot interrupt another position. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only; cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases.

Trade ships are not exhausted. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency's Writers box; dividers preserve affiliation and then return to supply. Filled tokens also return to supply.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade; Upkeep and Refresh

answers.answer: At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request President treasury funds for printed-price local alliances in the Army; President must approve. Move purchased alliances to top/active half. Deploy/defense exhausts the whole alliance to bottom; its printed strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split between purposes. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too and never reactivates alliances.

Company defense penalty is zero and the controlled region has no tower, so it earns zero tower trophies. For reopening orders or clearing unrest, with no tower or faceup loot modifier, use minimum loot equal to surviving participating officers plus one for Commander, distributed by normal payout procedure.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — deploying in Company region

answers.answer: Two successful Build actions total are needed: first success places partial ship in Governor's region if absent; a later success completes it to the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. Each successful Build is one stage. Commissioned regiments go into that President's Army; they have officer-like strength, loot is paid to bank, and they do not roll officer-loss checks.

China is created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director may transfer ships there like any sea zone. It acts after Bengal; its ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.
answers.evidence: Director of Trade; Superintendent of Trade in China

answers.answer: China cannot retry: it attempts only once, even if failed. Do not attempt without an export icon in Company-controlled regions. Roll one die per ship; on success count export icons only in Company-controlled regions, pay Company Balance £4 per icon and Superintendent's family £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company exports do not count; Company payment is not flat £4.

When Governor General law creates the office, make Governors pensioners, remove overlays and partial ships, and return Governor/Director cards to box. Replace Director of Trade with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and place ribbon overlay. Later conquests create no Governors/overlays; printed Company symbols indicate control. Governor General hires Presidents and occupies former Director's treasury/turn position, rolls attrition normally; Region Loss skips Governor Elimination.

First add £3 Balance per Company region. Then Govern repeatedly, spending £1 treasury per die with no penalty, at most one successful Govern per turn. Every rolled 6 adds one unrest to every Company region, even on success; failure adds one more unrest in every Company region. On success receive £1 per Company region and choose one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone (China included), add a regiment to any Army, or add £2 to Balance/any office treasury except own while adding unrest to a Company region. Unrest from multiple Tax choices must be placed in different regions.

Roll once per eligible player-owned ship: 1–2 no effect; 3–4 fatigue it, or sink it if already fatigued; 5–6 sink it. Sunk ship returns to its shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count as Eastern. Firm ships use strategy zone; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Player ships in Company fleets are checked in affected zones.

When an order closes, return its writer to owner's supply; when a filled token is encountered, flip it to closed. If a requested close is in a fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region's orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order; if none, it also Cascades. A region can initiate Cascade only once per event tile, though it can receive multiple Cascades.

Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region, or Cascades if all closed. Windfall gives owners £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle: March the Elephant, then shuffle this event into the remaining draw stack and separately shuffle discards and put them on top. If draw stack is empty, March last instead.

Leader: top-stack sovereign region gains one tower; a dominated region instead rebels using printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

If Elephant is on a border, open orders connected across that border and add a tower to each touched non-Company region. If fully within a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March the Elephant.

For ordinary non-Company Invasion, compare attacker's whole empire strength plus event modifier against defender's whole empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater. On success replace defender flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking capital shatters its empire. If attacker lacked an empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none available, no flags/new empire form. Equal is failure; attacker loses one tower.

For Rebellion, only rebelling region strength plus modifier counts against its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. Rebel must be strictly greater, so a tie fails. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.

On Region Loss, Commander returns half family's trophies rounded up and returns to supply. Roll one die per officer in associated Army; each 6 removes it. Eliminate Governor (card to unused stack, fatigue/member to supply), remove overlay, partial ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion's specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to region with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up. Future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses Presidency association. Close orders for Invasion Crisis, cascading if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals regions lost so far this turn: first -1, second additional -2, etc. A loss does not automatically remove any other region; each attack/defense resolves separately.

After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise to top-stack region. Put it fully inside a Company region; in a dominated region point toward sovereign; in a sovereign region point across shape-marked border on tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated; if all are, use redirect-arrow border toward empire capital.

Roll storm die for target direction: West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all storms targets each, none targets top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary attack die and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Unrest adds nothing to primary Foreign Invasion attack or tower calculation; Company-defense secondary unrest attacks still apply.
answers.evidence: Events — Foreign Invasion; FAQ & Rulings — Foreign Invasion and unrest

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws, may stop or draw up to three total; choose any revealed one and discard the rest. Drawing a dilemma forces choosing it immediately and ends drawing. Before voting, PM rotates dial clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching chosen law's bottom icon; that space fixes target and consequence. Read law and set Vote marker to its printed starting support.

Tax: each family pays bank £1 per target it owns; unpaid target returns to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each family member's prize; return enterprise/prize member if unpaid. Lost shipyards leave fitted ships in play and unavailable until ship returns; lost prizes/luxuries lose VP. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per owned target. Power: swap target marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.

Starting with PM and clockwise, each player casts votes; each £1 family cash buys one vote plus card votes. A card's votes can be used only once in the entire vote across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave rotated until resolution. After each full round PM may call another or stop; a round with no votes must end voting.

A player who voted for may later oppose; after opposing, cannot vote for in this vote. Track opposition; largest opponent holds Opposition Leader, ties leave current holder in place. With recipient consent, votes can be cast for a player who already opposed or commits to oppose and add to that player's opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of 'Vote with my enterprises' promise. At resolution restore used cards to regular orientation.

Pay upkeep separately for each family member on a prize, including final turn. If unpaid, return member and lose that prize's printed VP; help may be negotiated while game continues. On nonfinal turns Refresh writers to associated Presidency Writers boxes, return filled tokens/dividers/extra ships to supply, reactivate exhausted Army officers/regiments, exhaust active alliances without reactivating them; fitted player ships retain fatigue. Final turn skips Refresh and goes to scoring.

Each shareholder gets one extra London Season retirement from supply (not Pensioners), regardless of firms owned. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts must be no more than the highest total dividend marker among firms where they own a share; printed cost can be higher if discount covers difference. Cannot retire from a firm with absent/zero marker. Discounts otherwise work normally. At Final Scoring, first score firms, then permit one such retirement regardless of Company survival/failure, before Power or ordinary scoring; no display cards.

Investment £5 comes from bank into London; trade revenue goes to India. London pays fitting, ship acquisition, bids and expenses; India pays dividends and expenses, and residual India cash sweeps into London. Family cash cannot transfer into or out of firm treasuries. Only specified investment, payout and expense procedures move firm money.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — firm treasuries; Firm expenses, rescue and dividends

answers.answer: Firms phase occurs if deregulated after Family/share creation and before Hiring: managers take investment actions without set order, then choose strategies. Manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; PM resolves between firms. Then strategies are selected.

A firm can fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 paid from London to bank with shipyard owner's consent. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent: £3 unfatigued or £2 fatigued, paid into Shipping treasury. It cannot acquire Company or extra ships. The summary does not expressly state fitting a different player's shipyard is possible beyond the consent rule; shipyard owner consent is required.

Only a player managing no firm may initiate a hostile takeover; managing another firm also disqualifies. Get consent of holders of a majority of target shares. Move target's ships, money and shares to own charter and copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

Managers negotiate and every shareholder must consent. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose. Transfer secondary shares, ships and treasury money to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Share transfers may be negotiated. If primary would exceed ten shares, return excess to their owners' supplies with those owners' consent. Primary retains its value/dividend track.
Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends, but still pays expenses and retains prior dividend marker for retirement; its firm ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade; Firm expenses, rescue and dividends

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investments use normal Company-share/workshop contribution rules, even if ten-share cap prevents additional shares: still put £5 from bank into London, pay expenses, lose any remaining cash and lower Value one space per emergency investment. The same-turn share restriction remains: shares created this turn cannot be used, even if traded away.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends; Firms phase — Invest

answers.answer: An emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. Normal merger procedure still applies, including consent of every involved shareholder. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.
Every shareholder must consent. Shares go to Debtor's Prison (each -1 VP); ships return to matching shipyards; charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for rest of game.

Before ordinary scoring, for each player add VP from all their shares across all firms and round that player's total down once, then deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. This firm step applies whether Company survives or fails. Fractional per-share rates by value: 1=-1, 2=0, 3–4=1/2, 5–7=1, 8–9=1 1/2, 10=2. Then eligible special retirement, Power, Court/workshops, and Company outcome step follow.
answers.evidence: Scoring — Final Scoring order; Firm-track VP per share

answers.answer: 1710 runs turns 1–5, starts monopoly and has no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs 3–7; starts monopoly and deregulation may be voted in. 1813 runs 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs 1–8 with deregulation available; its initial position matches 1710.

1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12, Debt 3, treasury £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship East Indian, and Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency. 1758 deregulation is available separately.

1813 starts at Standing £10/Debt 0, £3 per office treasury; laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Place +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return Governor General law to box and put Governor General overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Copy India map from scenario card reverse.

Power awards are 3 VP first/1 second for final turn 1–3, 5/2 for 4–6, 8/4 for 7–8. If first place is tied, each tied player gets only the lower award (1, 2 or 4 VP respectively); no other award is made.

Initial Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping and Manufacturing 0. In 1758/Long 1710, Deregulation vote may be called if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and is mandatory if either is starred. Standing expectations run £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; reset S is above £10. Deregulation Standing lined at £4/6/8 (star at £4), Debt lined 5/6/7/8 (star at 8).

No. The ordinary die roll supplies Foreign Invasion's primary strength and the resulting tower level is half that roll rounded down; unrest does not modify either. On success close all target orders once, cascading if already all closed; Region Loss does not close them again. Secondary unrest attacks still use Company-defense procedure.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings — Foreign Invasion and unrest

answers.answer: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and take from bank only cash equal to actual Balance reduction, not more than available Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to officer, then appoints a Commander from officers; the same former Commander remains eligible for reappointment.

Set Balance to £5, Power tokens to indicated positions and family VP markers to zero. Put local alliances in named Army boxes and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose scenario and use its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and political map; put Turn marker on scenario's start date and PM dial arm to matching date. Exact India towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant come from scenario card (and player holdings from dealt setup cards).

Normal order: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation vote is at turn start before London Season. Skip London Season on the first game turn.

If Chairman office is vacant, former Chairman acts first; then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each Pensioner to a prize, paying its printed cost, moving member to prize and gaining printed VP. Set actual spending aside to determine display-selection priority after all retirements, then pay bank. Pensioners need not all retire, but unused ones do not last: return all Pensioners to supplies at end of London Season.

No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital's starred flag so it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.

The Chairman title holder takes the first Family action; players then act clockwise. After every player resolves their family action, if Debt and applicants remain, create shares by moving rightmost applicants into Court one at a time and lowering Debt one each, until either applicants or Debt run out.

Sequence is Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay President → Madras President → Bengal President → China Superintendent if created. Skip a vacant office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring. Newly created offices normally await Hiring, except China Superintendent is immediately hired when created.

answers.answer: Begin by rolling storm die: its face identifies affected zones and number of India events. Resolve all storms before drawing events. Then flip and resolve tiles one at a time for the indicated count. Company/extra ships never storm-check; eligible player ships in affected zones roll once each, China counts Eastern, firm ships count in strategy zone and Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Ship storm results are 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue or sink if fatigued, 5–6 sink. No storm indication means no checks; three storms checks all zones.

For an ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, the tail is attacker/acting region and head is defender. A sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) makes an Invasion; a dominated actor (small flag or no dome) rebels against its sovereign. Elephant fully inside a Company region means Rebellion against Company. This classifier is for ordinary Crisis, not Foreign Invasion. Sovereign/domination is identified by flag/dome status as described: sovereign regions have dome without flag or capital/star flag; dominated regions have small flag or no dome.
answers.evidence: India terminology; Events — Choose the ordinary Crisis procedure from the Elephant
